title: Auth setup project
summary: Write auth.setup.ts: sign in once and save the browser state to playwright/.auth/user.json. A provided dashboard test reuses it.
why: Logging in through the UI before every test is slow, and every test fails when login breaks. A setup project logs in once; every other test starts already signed in.
objectives: setup('…', async ({ page }) => { … }) using test as setup
Wait for the dashboard URL before saving
hints: import { test as setup, expect } from '@playwright/test';
The hub config runs *.setup.ts in a 'setup' project that the main project depends on.
pitfalls: Saving state before the login redirect finished → the file has no session cookie.
Committing playwright/.auth to git — it contains real session cookies.
teachAlong: Cause: setup saves cookies + localStorage once.
Effect: dependent tests start signed in.
Gate: the provided dashboard test must pass using your saved file.

requires.reason: Save the session: await page.context().storageState({ path: authFile }).
Wait for the login to finish (await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/dashboard$/)) before saving, or the state may miss the session cookie.

wrongSolutions.label: logs in but never saves
